claims.statement: Private-action test tutorial expects greeting/input and output timestamp in selected latest run's job/steps. Expected log text is not a real execution receipt or proof of action behavior.

Third-party template action is not GitHub-certified and has separate terms/privacy/support. Commit SHA recommended for stable/security-sensitive references; tags/branches can change without warning, requiring deliberate SHA update. Certification not implied by Marketplace existence.

Docker, JavaScript and composite actions need YAML metadata action.yml or action.yaml defining inputs/outputs/runs; action.yml preferred. File presence is not semantic behavior or valid implementation proof.

For ephemeral runners with automatic updates disabled, upgrade runners to target GHES app version before instance upgrade or risk offline runners. Conditional lifecycle guidance is not permission to disable updates or upgrade instance.
OIDC subject template customization uses request-body configuration to organization/repository API endpoints. Schema/authority/trust approval remain separately reviewed; no request submitted.

Reusable examples show external same-repo SHA, local ./ and $/ caller-commit references (the latter unavailable GHES), and other-repo v1 tag. Version examples are not immutable policy or actual workflow invocation.
org/my-group and ent/my-group distinguish same-name groups with conjunctive self-hosted/label-1 requirements. Scope qualification resolves ambiguity, not granting access or actual matching capacity.
Variable UI takes Name and Value fields; values are not inherently secret-safe, and no variable created.

Metrics UI selects usage/performance, optional period/tab filters with qualifier/operator/value, applies them and optionally downloads CSV. Actual metric data, completeness and permission availability remain separate.

Workflow tutorial stores YAML under .github/workflows, configures push/ubuntu-latest/Node24 checkout and bats installation/version, then commits/pushes. Inert example and installed file do not prove successful execution or authorize dependencies.

Annotated example distinguishes workflow name fallback, actor-based run-name, push trigger, job ID, runner, steps, checkout, Node PATH and shell commands. Latest stable runner is not newest vendor OS; includes/links separately resolved.

Diagram caption describes hierarchy and four steps but image not visually reviewed. Workflow activity navigation includes repository/Actions/workflow/run links and job/step display; visualized expected activity is not actual receipt.

Dispatch example declares required choice logLevel with info/warning/debug defaultwarning, Boolean print_tags, string tags and environment selection; condition uses typed Boolean. Environment input alone does not reference job deployment environment.
Example directly interpolates user tags into shell echo, which requires script-injection review under the separately reviewed untrusted-input guidance; not accepted safe template or executed.
Dispatch inputs arrive in inputs context with separately included typing/limit comparison to github.event.inputs. Inclusion is not independent rendered completeness.
workflow_dispatch accepts optional inputs and receives trigger events only when workflow file is on default branch; not a universal default-branch restriction for all event types.
Repository token defaults can be restricted or permissive; capability to choose does not establish least privilege, effective defaults or authorized change.
Repository writers can edit workflow permissions to add/remove token rights; actual granted rights remain bounded by higher policies/fork/event constraints rather than unrestricted escalation.
Workflow PR creation/approval can be allowed or prevented; setting capability is not actual grant, branch-protection satisfaction or authority to self-approve.
workflow_ref is workflow path with ref, example owner/repository/file@refs/heads branch. It is a description of identity, not reusable-call syntax permitting those prefixes.
Workflow-approval link references applicable policy procedure, not an approval receipt or reviewed linked body.

Public fork workflow approval may depend on PR creator OR triggering user; default first-time contributors need approval. pull_request_target base-context runs regardless of these settings. Generic no-secret prose must remain qualified by privileged-event exceptions.
Approval policy primarily limits unwanted compute execution; approved/bypassing untrusted code still executes on self-hosted infrastructure, so approval does not certify isolation or code safety.

Untrusted workflow_run code risks cache poisoning and unintended writes/secrets access; privileged follow-on trigger must not be treated safe merely because predecessor checks ran. Linked mitigation remains separate review.
